title: The bait mode's wave, second pass: no ball, the Reeds and the boss come up out of a tremor at the centre, the Reeds' solver at 120 Hz above ten, low-poly carcasses that decay
context: Owner, 2026-10-10: "1) hide the ball in bait mode, 3) Have the Reed and the boss come out of a tremor in the center. 4) try with 20 reed. 5) could we start with 120 HZ when there are more than 10 Reeds, and switch back to 240HZ when there are fewer? 6) we need a low-poly dead Reed Carcass that stays and decays." Follows 2026-10-10-boss-bait-first-wave-reeds. Bait mode only; the tank mode, src/sentry-pilot.js, the game's src/fx and the ported kit src/fx/nih-dairia untouched.
outcome: THE BALL: the Reeds' kits draw no prey (createNihDairia makes none); the one prey mesh is the boss's, and the lab showed it whenever the lure was not 'tank', so a lure left on point or auto in the tank mode drew it at Isao's ground point in the bait mode. It is now drawn in the tank mode only. THE EMERGENCE (src/domain/boss-wave.js emergePlan, emergence, keepOut; BOSS_FIGHT.wave.emerge { gap 0.6, lead 0.35, rise 1.5, depth 1.15, jitter 4, fan 20, fanFor 2.5, keep 25 }): every Reed is made 4 m off the arena's centre and waits below the ground, hidden and unstepped; its turn comes 0.6 s of the lab's clock after the one before (the lab's, not the wave's slowed clock: at 20 Reeds the wave's clock runs x0.2 and a wave-clock schedule took 34 s to bring them all up); a tremor (the seat's camera turned by up to 2.5 % of the lens's field times the trauma squared, the main view only, the pilot's pose untouched; the back mouth's 'rock.dust' round the point, the boss's 'mortar.shell'; the breach's sinkhole_quake low-passed at 420 Hz, at most once in 3 s for the Reeds: audio-defaults.js has no rumble, the game's tremor sound is src/content/breach-defaults.js's), then the drawing rises over 1.5 s from 1.15 times the rest height below while the body stands on its own floor with its motion off (the body is never moved, so the solver has nothing to resolve: no body thrown, every Reed within 4 m of the centre when up), then it walks to its fan point (20 m out, the directions a golden angle apart) for at most 2.5 s of the wave's clock and hunts. A Reed not up is no body for the rules. The boss comes up the same way after the last Reed dies (17.3 m deep, motion off and out of the fight's reach until up). Isao's planner is kept 25 m off the centre while a Reed is still to come up and 45 m while the boss rises, through the lab's clamp and hold (keepOut) and, for a fly-over the hold does not touch, a put-out after his step. THE STEP (waveStep; coarse { on, above 10, hz 120 }, the panel's switch): the kit's FixedStepper takes its step at construction and keeps it in a closure, but each fixed step simulates the creature's own phys.step, read live; so the lab sets kit.phys.step and hands update dt x (1/240) / step: the stepper's 1/240 s count becomes 1/120 s steps, no change in the kit. The solver's velocity is (x - previous) / h of each step, so a change of h carries no jolt. THE CARCASSES (carcassLook; carcass { decay 60, max 30, dark 0.75, flat 0.4, sink 0.35, cold 0.6 }): 2 s after a death (and 0.4 s of the wave's clock of collapse, 6 s at most) the Reed is laid down as its tet cage's outer surface (the faces of one tet only, wound outward, over the solver's nodes in the pose it collapsed to: 1,584 triangles against the skin's 18,812), flat shaded in the skin's mean tissue colour, in the frame it was drawn in; its solver, wasm kernel, skin, fear and temperament go. Over 60 s it darkens toward a dark brown, flattens to 0.4 of its height and sinks 0.35 of it; in the seat's thermal its own emissive starts at the heat tagging's warm (0.55) and is cold by 60 % of the decay (the carcasses are not in the thermal's warm parts, which would hold them warm); then it goes; at most 30 lie; R clears them. A material and a transform a frame each; they block nothing and are no one's target. MEASURED (headless Chrome, the seat's thermal, the fight off for a stable field, every Reed up, 6 s each; the wave held to its 10 ms solver budget, so the solver ms is pinned and the Reeds' clock is the cost): 5 Reeds: 240 Hz 48.3 fps, clock x0.59 (1/120 forced: x0.99); 10 Reeds: 240 Hz 47.7 fps, x0.27 (1/120 forced: 43.6 fps, x0.43); 20 Reeds: the rule on (120 Hz) 45.3 fps, x0.22, 0.87 ms a step; off (240 Hz) 43.1 fps, x0.12, 0.78 ms a step; 50 Reeds at 120 Hz: ~41-42 fps, x0.078 (x0.044-0.048 at 240 Hz before). At 5 and 10 the rule's on and off are the same (240 Hz). A 1/120 s step costs ~10-15 % more than a 1/240 s one but there are half as many: the Reeds run about 1.8 times as fast for the same solver ms. THE SWITCH: traced at 20 -> 11 -> 10 Reeds, the fastest live node (local m/s; the kit's 7 cm body scaled 85 times in space and not in time, so limb tips read hundreds of m/s) over the 60 frames before the switch max 441.7 / mean 229.3, after it max 293.7 / mean 192.0; the frames round it 190.9, 178.2, 241.3, 208.9 | 221.7, 201.2, 250.0: no spike. At 120 Hz the Reeds look as at 240 Hz in the seat and ISAO · CAM (whole limbs, no inverted tets).
alternatives: A hook in the kit (expose the creature's FixedStepper, or read P.step in it) for the step switch (rejected: the stepper is a pure accumulator, and scaling the dt the lab hands it gives the same steps with the kit unchanged)

Lifting the body's nodes out of the ground with the drawing (rejected: nodes under the floor are what the contact solve pushes out, the one way to throw a body; the drawing alone rises while the body stands settled on its floor)
The emergence on the wave's slowed clock (tried first: 20 Reeds took 34 s of real time to come up at x0.2; the turns and the rise are the player's, on the lab's clock)
The skin's own surface frozen as the carcass (rejected: 18,812 triangles each, against the cage's 1,584; and the brief asked for low-poly)
Twenty Reeds by default (not done: the brief measured 20; the count stays 10, ?reeds=20 and the slider try it; at 20 the wave's clock is x0.22, close to ten's x0.27)
evidence: node --check on every edited file; npm test (226 programs; test/boss-wave.mjs extended: emergePlan, emergence, waveStep, carcassLook, keepOut and the new content), npm run check, npm run build green
from an APFS snapshot, sequentially, one headless Chrome (memory WARN on swap): --boss-wave (extended) green, --boss-friends green, --boss green

--boss-wave: the lure left on point in the tank mode, no prey mesh shown in the bait mode during the wave or with the boss; ten Reeds each first seen 4.0 m from the centre, nine of ten first seen below and all with their top 0.84 m under the surface before rising (below>tremor>rising>up), each 4.0 m from the centre when up, 10 shakes (peak 0.29 degrees), Isao never nearer than 30.9 m while the keep-out held (25 m), 240 Hz at ten; the hunt closed 34.4 m on where Isao was over 8 s (he keeps his distance); 40 mm and 25 mm kills laid down as 1,584-triangle carcasses; killReeds(): the boss's tremor and rise from 17.3 m down, the lift climbing, Isao at 45 m; the boss shown, stepping, 180/180; 10 carcasses lying; the decay shortened to 6 s: a carcass's heat 0.56 -> 0, its height 0.91 -> 0.40, then gone; R: ten again, no carcass; 20 Reeds at 1/120 s (45.4 fps, x0.22), thinned to 11 still 1/120 s, at 10 back at 1/240 s, no jolt; 50 Reeds all up

screenshots (scratchpad): emerge.png (the seat's thermal over the centre: Reeds coming up in a warm cluster with the dust round them, ISAO · CAM on the cluster), carcasses.png (the boss risen at the centre among warm low-poly carcasses; ISAO · CAM over a faceted carcass under the boss), reeds-120hz.png and reeds-240hz.png (20 Reeds round a still Isao: the same bodies, x0.20 against x0.10)
